entries.regional_usage_notes: US: a soft, bread-like roll. UK: a crisp or hard baked snack (US cookie or cracker).
US: the paved road surface. UK: the footpath beside a road (US sidewalk).
US: American football. UK: association football (US soccer).
US: trousers. UK: underwear.
US: a sleeveless dress, or a person who jumps. UK: a knitted pullover (US sweater).
US: straps holding up trousers (UK braces). UK: fasteners holding up stockings.
US: a waistcoat. UK: an undershirt.
US: to postpone discussion of a motion. UK: to put a motion forward for discussion.
US: plain or unattractive in appearance. UK: comfortable and cosy.
US: the teaching staff of a university. UK: a major division of a university (for example the Faculty of Law).
US: a university or higher-education institution. UK: a school for ages 16 and over, or a constituent part of a university.
US: the fee charged for teaching. UK: teaching or instruction itself.
US: an administrative officer keeping academic records. UK: a hospital doctor in specialist training.
US: an adviser, often in business. UK: a senior hospital doctor.
US: a scientist who studies chemistry. UK: also a pharmacist or the pharmacy shop.
Both: an operation. UK: also a doctor’s or dentist’s consulting room.
US: often a secret or dishonest plan. UK: a neutral word for a plan or programme.
US: unnecessary or superfluous. UK: also dismissed from a job because the work is no longer needed.
US: unnecessary repetition. UK: also dismissal from a job because the work is no longer needed.
US: usually the rate at which employees leave. UK: usually a company’s revenue from sales.
US: an underground railway. UK: an underground pedestrian passage.
US: a handbag. UK: a small bag or wallet for money.
US: often means very. UK: often means fairly or somewhat.
UK: a lawyer who advises clients and prepares cases. US: a government law officer, or a person who solicits.
US: a burning flame on a stick. UK: a handheld electric lamp (US flashlight).
US: a woman’s or baby’s hat. UK: the hinged cover over a car engine (US hood).
US: footwear. UK: also the luggage compartment of a car (US trunk).
US: thin fried slices of potato (UK crisps). UK: fried strips of potato (US fries).
US: a fruit spread (UK jam). UK: a gelatine dessert (US Jell-O).
US: a folding camp bed. UK: a baby’s bed (US crib).
US: usually unfermented apple juice. UK: an alcoholic drink made from apples.
US: a formal school dance. UK: a seafront promenade or a promenade concert.
